from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

        "Allowlisting runs only approved applications.",

scenarios.title: The 99% model that fails in production
scenarios.context: Your classifier scores 99% in validation but 61% on live data. Something is wrong with the evaluation, not the world.

steps.prompt: What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Data leakage - preprocessing fit on the full dataset before the split
options.why: Scaling or encoding fit before splitting leaks test information into training - validation scores become fiction.

options.text: The model is underfitting
options.why: Underfitting shows low scores everywhere, not a 99-to-61 collapse.

options.text: The learning rate is too high
options.why: A bad learning rate hurts training too - it does not create a validation/production gap.

options.text: Too little training data
options.why: Small data hurts all scores roughly equally; the gap pattern points to leakage.

options.text: Put every preprocessing step inside a pipeline, inside the cross-validation fold
options.why: Pipelines refit preprocessing per fold - no information crosses the train/validation boundary.

options.text: Collect more data and retrain the same way
options.why: More data with the same leakage just produces more confident fiction.

options.text: Switch to a deeper neural network
options.why: Model complexity does not fix an evaluation methodology bug.

options.text: Tune hyperparameters on the test set
options.why: Tuning on the test set is itself leakage - the test set must stay held out.

steps.prompt: How do you verify the fix worked?

options.text: Evaluate once on a held-out test set that never touched training or tuning
options.why: A truly held-out test set is the only honest estimate of production performance.

options.text: Re-run the same cross-validation and trust it
options.why: CV you already tuned against is optimistic - you need untouched data.

options.text: Check training accuracy
options.why: Training accuracy measures memorization, not generalization.

options.text: Ask stakeholders if the number looks right
options.why: Plausibility is not evidence - measure on held-out data.

scenarios.title: Grounding answers in changing product docs
scenarios.context: Support needs an assistant that answers from product documentation that updates weekly. You must choose the architecture.

steps.prompt: RAG or fine-tuning for weekly-changing docs?

options.text: RAG - retrieve the current docs at query time, then generate grounded on them
options.why: RAG handles frequently changing knowledge without retraining; fine-tuning bakes in knowledge that goes stale.

options.text: Fine-tune weekly on the new docs
options.why: Weekly fine-tuning is expensive, slow, and still cannot cite sources.

options.text: Prompt the base model harder
options.why: Prompting cannot inject knowledge the model never saw.

options.text: Train a model from scratch on the docs
options.why: Massively disproportionate cost for a retrieval problem.

steps.prompt: Answers must cite their sources. Which chunking choice helps?

options.text: Parent-child chunks: retrieve small passages, cite the parent section
options.why: Small chunks retrieve precisely; parent context keeps citations traceable to the real document section.

options.text: One giant chunk per document
options.why: Giant chunks dilute retrieval precision and waste context.

options.text: No chunking - embed whole PDFs
options.why: Whole-document embeddings blur the specific passage the answer needs.

options.text: Random chunk boundaries
options.why: Arbitrary boundaries split coherent passages and break citation quality.

steps.prompt: How do you evaluate the system honestly?

options.text: A golden question-answer set scored for groundedness and citation accuracy
options.why: Fixed evals with groundedness checks measure what matters: correct, cited answers - not vibes.

options.text: Ask the team if answers look good
options.why: Eyeballing does not catch regressions or hallucinations systematically.

options.text: Count how fast it responds
options.why: Latency matters, but speed says nothing about correctness.

options.text: Trust the demo - it worked once
options.why: One good demo is not evidence; evals are.

scenarios.title: The prediction-drift alert fires
scenarios.context: Monitoring flags prediction drift on your production model: the output distribution shifted this week. Revenue-facing decisions depend on it.

options.text: Whether the input data distribution shifted (data drift) or the input-output relationship changed (concept drift)
options.why: The distinction decides the fix: shifted inputs may need pipeline repair; a changed relationship needs retraining on fresh labels.

options.text: Restart the serving containers
options.why: Restarts fix infrastructure, not statistical drift.

options.text: Immediately retrain on all historical data
options.why: Retraining without diagnosing wastes the chance to find the real cause - and may bake in the problem.

options.text: Disable monitoring to stop the alerts
options.why: Silencing the smoke detector during a fire.

steps.prompt: Diagnosis: concept drift - the relationship itself changed. What now?

options.text: Retrain on freshly labeled data reflecting the new relationship, with a holdout for validation
options.why: Concept drift means old labels encode the old world - only fresh labels teach the new one.

options.text: Keep the old model; drift always reverts

steps.prompt: How do you ship the retrained model safely?

options.text: Shadow or canary deployment with a rollback plan before full cutover
options.why: Progressive delivery proves the new model on live traffic with a safe retreat - the production discipline.

options.text: Replace the model file directly in production
options.why: Big-bang swaps with no rollback turn every retrain into a gamble.

options.text: Ship it Friday evening to avoid traffic
options.why: Low traffic means slow detection of problems - and nobody around to roll back.

options.text: Skip evaluation; the training loss looked good
options.why: Training loss never validated a production model.

blocks.body: Precision: of predicted positives, how many were right (punishes false alarms). Recall: of actual positives, how many were found (punishes misses). F1: harmonic mean.
Imbalanced data: 99% accuracy is trivial when 99% of labels are negative. Match the metric to the business cost.
Train fits, validation tunes, test estimates - exactly once, held out from everything.
Queries match keys to weight values; positional encodings restore order. Parallel across the sequence - that is why it replaced recurrence.
GPT: autoregressive next-token prediction (generative). BERT: masked-token prediction (understanding).
Retrieve relevant chunks, generate grounded on them. Choose RAG when knowledge changes often and answers must cite sources; fine-tune for stable behavior change.
LoRA: freeze the base model, train low-rank adapters (rank, alpha). QLoRA: 4-bit base plus adapters - big models on one GPU.
Think, act, observe, repeat - until the goal or a step bound. Watch for loops, drift, cost blowups.
One open standard between AI apps and tools/data/workflows: hosts and clients call servers exposing tools, resources, prompts.
RLHF: reward model on preference pairs, then PPO. DPO: preference objective directly, no reward model, no RL loop.
Data drift: input distribution shifts. Concept drift: the input-to-label relationship changes - retrain on fresh labels.
Shadow: score live traffic without serving. Canary: small slice. Blue-green: full cutover, instant rollback.
GPU-hours and tokens dominate. Batching and caching are the cheapest optimizations; quantization trades precision for memory and latency.
Zero grads first - stale gradients are a silent bug.

answerBank.q: What does this academy prepare you for?
answerBank.a: The full AI-engineer spine: Python, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, NLP, agentic systems, Azure AI, and production MLOps - ending in one deployed capstone. Preparation only, conferring no certificate.

answerBank.q: Is this course affiliated with Microsoft or Simplilearn?
answerBank.a: No. It is distilled from the public shape of the Microsoft + Simplilearn AI Engineer program, with original exposition throughout - not affiliated with either, and vendor documentation is the anchor, never the copy.

answerBank.q: Does completing this academy confer a certificate?
answerBank.a: No. Preparation only - this course confers no certificate. Vendor certification exams are taken through the vendor's own portal.

answerBank.q: When should I choose RAG over fine-tuning?
answerBank.a: Choose RAG when knowledge updates frequently and answers must cite sources - retrieve, then generate. Choose fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA/QLoRA) when behavior must change permanently on stable data.
The distance between modeling and operating: a trained model is not a system. Production demands serving, monitoring, drift response, cost control, evaluation harnesses, and rollback plans.

answerBank.q: Which exam does the Azure path map to?
answerBank.a: Microsoft's AI-900 (Azure AI Fundamentals): the Azure AI service catalog, ML concepts in Microsoft's vocabulary, responsible AI, and cost/governance/compliance scenarios.
